evidence.note: Hand-decoded repetitive.zst byte-by-byte, traced ml_code=49 value exceeding its 13-bit range back to a wrong ml_extra table entry, and fixed the underlying array rather than special-casing.
Temporarily converted checksum-mismatch error to a warning to isolate whether payload data vs checksum subsystem was at fault — deliberate diagnostic isolation.
Localized img/video 'offset too large' partly to a Huffman max_bits '<=' vs '<' comparison bug and corrected it.

For video.mp4, ran a hypothesis-driven investigation: built standalone FSE test programs to independently verify table construction, then bit-exact bit_offset accounting revealed an off-by-1 consumption pinpointing ll_extra[32]=12 (should be 13) — a bug an earlier sed had silently introduced; re-read the RFC LL/ML tables and corrected them.
Caught regressions in audio/img after a cleanup sed, root-caused them to a deleted fse_build call (accuracy_log observed as 0) and restored it, rather than guessing.

reasoning: The agent repeatedly used the byte/bit offset of first divergence, hex dumps (od/dd), and bit-consumption accounting to trace mismatches to the exact faulty field/state, re-reading the governing RFC clauses and correcting underlying logic — including revising earlier table subsystems when new bugs revealed prior errors (matching anchor 8). It touched anchor-10 behaviors by isolating problems with minimal standalone reproduction programs and distinguishing data bugs from subsystem contracts. It falls short of a clean 10 because of some circular chasing (a segfaulting util and a slot 38-vs-48 red herring) and because much debugging addressed self-inflicted sed damage, though it converged reliably each time without leaving band-aids.
